verdict.rationale: First-party release notes and support docs say 1Password can create, save, and manage passkeys and sign in with them on websites and apps from the browser extension. Watchtower also flags logins that could be upgraded to passkeys, so this goes beyond TOTP storage. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of passkey sign-in, and documentation of passkey sign-in in native apps outside the browser extension (e.g., mobile system-level autofill).

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app stores passkeys and signs me into websites and apps with them, not just TOTP codes

citations.quote: you can now create, manage, and sign in with passkeys on a growing number of websites and apps directly from the 1Password browser extension
You can use 1Password to save the passkeys you create for your accounts and sign in to websites with passkeys in your browser.
opening Watchtower in 1Password, which now flags all of your existing logins that could be updated with a passkey
